prompt: A company used to trust any device connected to its office network. Under its new policy, every request to a corporate app is authenticated and authorized using the user's identity, location, device health and the sensitivity of the data, even when the request comes from inside the office. Which Zero Trust principle does this policy apply?

options.text: Verify explicitly
Use least privileged access
Defense in depth
Assume breach

explanation: Verify explicitly means always authenticating and authorizing based on all available signals, such as identity, location, device health, the service and the data classification, instead of trusting the network a request comes from. Least privileged access limits how much access is granted, with just-in-time and just-enough access. Assume breach is about segmenting access and limiting the blast radius. Defense in depth is a layered strategy, not one of the three Zero Trust principles.

prompt: A developer is deciding where to use encryption and where to use hashing in a new app. Which TWO statements about hashing are true? (Select TWO.)

options.text: The length of the hash grows with the length of the input
The same input always produces the same hash value
Hashing uses a public key to hash data and a private key to reverse it
Both sides need the same shared secret key to reverse a hash
The original text can't be recovered from the hash

explanation: A hash function is deterministic and one-way: the same input gives the same fixed-length output, and there's no key that turns it back into the input. That's why passwords are stored as salted hashes and checked by hashing what the user types. Public and private key pairs belong to asymmetric encryption, and a shared secret key belongs to symmetric encryption. The hash length is set by the algorithm, whatever the size of the input.

prompt: A retailer collects customer data in Brazil, stores it in a datacenter in the United States and processes it in Ireland. Its lawyers warn that the data is subject to the laws of each of those countries. Which concept describes this?

options.text: Data sovereignty
Data classification
Data residency
Data privacy

explanation: Data sovereignty is the idea that data is subject to the laws and regulations of each country or region where it's collected, held or processed, so one data set can fall under several jurisdictions at once. Data residency rules govern where data may be physically stored and when it can be transferred. Data privacy is about handling personal data properly, and data classification labels data by sensitivity.

prompt: Employees of a partner company need to use a project portal that a manufacturer hosts. The manufacturer's identity provider is set up to trust sign-ins from the partner's identity provider, so partner employees use their own work accounts and the manufacturer never stores their passwords. What is this arrangement called?

options.text: Federation
Directory synchronization
Role-based access control
Single sign-on within one identity provider

explanation: Federation is a trust relationship between identity providers: the manufacturer accepts the partner's authentication, so users sign in with their home accounts and the resource side never handles their credentials. The trust can go in one direction only. Directory synchronization copies identities from one directory into another. Single sign-on within one identity provider doesn't cross organizations, and role-based access control decides what a signed-in user may do, not where they authenticate.

prompt: A company's on-premises domain controllers authenticate users with Kerberos, organize computers into organizational units and push settings to them with Group Policy. Which service provides these capabilities?

options.text: Microsoft Intune
Active Directory Domain Services
Microsoft Entra ID
Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync

explanation: AD DS is the on-premises directory service in Windows Server: domain controllers authenticate users with Kerberos or NTLM, and admins organize objects into organizational units and manage them with Group Policy. Microsoft Entra ID is a cloud identity provider built around modern protocols such as OpenID Connect, OAuth and SAML, without OUs or Group Policy. Cloud Sync only synchronizes identities from AD DS to Entra ID, and Intune manages devices from the cloud.

prompt: An app running on an Azure virtual machine needs to read secrets from Azure Key Vault. The security team doesn't want any credential stored in the app's code or configuration, and wants the identity removed automatically if the VM is deleted. What should the developers use?

options.text: A system-assigned managed identity enabled on the virtual machine itself
A guest user account invited to the tenant for the app
A user-assigned managed identity shared by several VMs
An app registration with a client secret in the app settings

explanation: Managed identities are service principals that Microsoft Entra ID manages for you, so no credential appears in code. A system-assigned identity is tied to one Azure resource and is deleted with it, which matches the requirement. A user-assigned identity is a separate resource that outlives the VMs using it and must be deleted explicitly. A client secret is exactly the stored credential the team wants to avoid, and guest accounts are for external people, not workloads.

prompt: A company is rolling out AI agents that act on their own to triage tickets and update records in business apps. It wants each agent to have its own identity in Microsoft Entra, with a designated human sponsor, Conditional Access based on the agent's risk and lifecycle governance. What should it use?

options.text: Guest user accounts created through B2B collaboration
A shared service account used by all the agents
Microsoft Entra Agent ID
One app registration with a single client secret for every agent

explanation: Microsoft Entra Agent ID provides agent identities: purpose-built identities for AI agents, distinct from traditional workload identities, that support Conditional Access based on agent risk and lifecycle governance with owners and sponsors. They cover agents acting for a user and agents acting on their own. A shared service account or one app registration for every agent makes it impossible to tell agents apart or govern them one by one, and B2B guest accounts are meant for external people.

prompt: A company with two Active Directory forests that aren't connected to each other wants its users to have one identity for on-premises and cloud apps. It wants Microsoft's recommended synchronization tool, with a lightweight agent and high availability through multiple agents. What should it deploy?

options.text: Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync
Microsoft Entra Domain Services
Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration
Microsoft Entra Connect Sync

explanation: Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync is the recommended tool for hybrid identity: a lightweight provisioning agent connects AD DS with Entra ID, the configuration lives in the cloud, several agents give high availability and disconnected multi-forest setups are supported. Connect Sync is the earlier on-premises sync server that Cloud Sync is replacing. B2B collaboration invites external users, and Entra Domain Services provides managed domain services in Azure rather than synchronizing your forests.

prompt: After a wave of adversary-in-the-middle phishing that stole one-time codes, a company wants to move its administrators to phishing-resistant authentication in Microsoft Entra ID. Which TWO methods qualify? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Hardware OATH tokens that show a new code every 30 seconds
SMS verification codes
Approving a push notification in Microsoft Authenticator
Passkeys (FIDO2), such as a FIDO2 security key
Windows Hello for Business

explanation: Passkeys and Windows Hello for Business sign a challenge with a private key that never leaves the device, and the credential is bound to the real sign-in service, so a look-alike page can't relay it. SMS and OATH codes can be typed into a fake page and replayed by the attacker in real time. Approving a push, even with number matching, only shows the user approved something, and an attacker relaying the sign-in can still get that approval.

prompt: A small nonprofit uses the free edition of Microsoft Entra ID and has no Conditional Access licenses. It wants all users to register for MFA, administrators to always use MFA and legacy authentication to be blocked, with as little setup as possible. What should it use?

options.text: Security defaults
Custom Conditional Access policies
Privileged Identity Management for all users
Microsoft Entra ID Protection risk policies

explanation: Security defaults are a preconfigured set of protections at no extra cost: MFA registration for everyone, MFA for administrators and for users when needed, and blocking of legacy authentication. They're meant for organizations on the free tier and are on by default in new tenants. Custom Conditional Access policies need Entra ID P1, while ID Protection risk policies and PIM need P2 or ID Governance licenses, so none of them fits this budget.

prompt: Users at a company called Fabrikam keep choosing passwords such as Fabrikam2026! or F@brikam1. Which Microsoft Entra feature blocks these passwords when users change or reset them?

options.text: A sign-in risk policy in Microsoft Entra ID Protection
Smart lockout thresholds for failed sign-ins
A custom banned password list in Password Protection
Self-service password reset with two required methods

explanation: Password Protection checks every new password against Microsoft's global banned password list plus a custom list where you add terms specific to the organization, such as its name, products or locations. Passwords are normalized first, so substitutions like @ for a are caught too. Smart lockout slows down guessing at sign-in, SSPR lets users reset forgotten passwords, and a sign-in risk policy reacts to suspicious sign-ins, but none of them rejects weak new passwords.

prompt: A company wants users to be prompted for MFA when they open the HR app from a device that isn't marked as compliant, and blocked entirely when they sign in from countries where it has no offices. Which Microsoft Entra feature enforces this?

options.text: Security defaults
Access reviews
Privileged Identity Management
Conditional Access

explanation: Conditional Access is the Zero Trust policy engine of Microsoft Entra ID: after first-factor authentication it evaluates signals such as the user, the app, device compliance and location, including named locations and countries, and then blocks access or grants it with requirements like MFA. PIM controls activation of privileged roles, access reviews periodically recertify who keeps access, and security defaults apply one fixed baseline that can't target a single app or country.

prompt: A help desk technician needs to reset passwords for regular users in Microsoft Entra ID, and nothing more. Following the principle of least privilege, which role should the technician get?

options.text: Security Reader
Global Administrator
Owner on the Azure subscription
Password Administrator

explanation: Password Administrator is a built-in Microsoft Entra role that can reset passwords for non-administrators and other Password Administrators, which covers the task without extra rights. Global Administrator can manage everything in the tenant, far more than needed. Owner is an Azure RBAC role over Azure resources such as VMs and storage, a separate system from Microsoft Entra roles. Security Reader can only view security information and can't reset anything.

prompt: Partners' guest accounts in a company's Microsoft Entra tenant keep their group memberships long after their projects end. The company wants group owners to confirm every quarter which guests still need access, and access removed when owners don't respond. What should it set up?

options.text: Recurring access reviews in Microsoft Entra ID Governance
User risk policies in Microsoft Entra ID Protection
A Conditional Access policy that requires MFA for guests
Dynamic membership rules based on the department attribute

explanation: Access reviews let owners, managers or the users themselves recertify group memberships, app access and role assignments on a schedule such as quarterly, and can automatically remove access that is denied or not reviewed. MFA for guests protects their sign-ins but doesn't remove access they no longer need. User risk policies react to compromised accounts, and dynamic rules depend on attributes that guest accounts usually don't keep up to date.

prompt: A company has six permanent Global Administrators and wants to reduce standing privilege with Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management (PIM). Which TWO capabilities does PIM provide for this? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Eligible assignments that admins activate just in time, for a limited period
Synchronization of admin accounts from on-premises AD DS
Detection of leaked credentials found on the dark web
Approval and a written justification required before a role is activated
Automatic blocking of sign-ins that come from anonymous IP addresses

explanation: PIM replaces permanent (active) role assignments with eligible ones: admins activate the role only when they need it, for a limited time, and activation can require approval, a justification, MFA and notifications, with an audit history of every activation. Leaked-credential and anonymous IP detections come from Microsoft Entra ID Protection, and synchronizing accounts from AD DS is the job of Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync or Connect Sync.

prompt: Microsoft finds a user's username and password in a credential dump posted online. The company wants that user to be forced to change their password securely the next time they sign in. Which feature detects this and can enforce the response?

options.text: Microsoft Entra access reviews, with a review of that user's groups
Microsoft Entra Password Protection, with the global banned list
Microsoft Entra ID Protection, with a user risk-based Conditional Access policy
Privileged Identity Management, with an alert on role activation

explanation: Leaked credentials are a user risk detection in Microsoft Entra ID Protection: they raise the probability that the account itself is compromised. A risk-based policy, usually built in Conditional Access, can then require a secure password change, with MFA, at the next sign-in. Password Protection only screens new passwords as they're set, access reviews recertify access on a schedule, and PIM governs privileged role activation.

prompt: A public web app runs behind Azure Application Gateway. It's receiving SQL injection attempts and, separately, large volumetric floods aimed at its public IP address. Which TWO services address these threats? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Azure Web Application Firewall on the Application Gateway
Azure DDoS Protection on the virtual network
A network security group that allows inbound traffic only on port 443
Azure Bastion deployed in the same virtual network
Azure Key Vault holding the app's connection strings

explanation: WAF inspects HTTP requests at layer 7 and blocks common exploits such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting, while Azure DDoS Protection mitigates volumetric attacks at layers 3 and 4 with tuned thresholds and telemetry. Microsoft recommends combining them, because neither covers the other's layer. Bastion provides RDP and SSH to VMs, Key Vault stores secrets, and an NSG allowing port 443 still lets both the injections and the flood through.

prompt: A company with a hub-and-spoke network in Azure wants one central, stateful service that filters traffic between its virtual networks and lets outbound web traffic reach only an approved list of fully qualified domain names (FQDNs). What should it deploy in the hub?

options.text: Azure Bastion
A network security group on each subnet
Azure Firewall
Azure DDoS Network Protection

explanation: Azure Firewall is a managed, stateful firewall as a service that you deploy centrally to filter traffic across virtual networks and subscriptions, with application rules based on FQDNs and threat intelligence filtering. NSGs filter by IP address, port and protocol at each subnet or network interface, but they can't filter by domain name and aren't a central service. DDoS Protection absorbs floods, and Bastion provides remote access to VMs.

prompt: An NSG on a subnet has two custom inbound rules: priority 200 denies RDP (port 3389) from any source, and priority 300 allows RDP from the administrator's IP address. What happens when the administrator tries to connect over RDP from that address?

options.text: It's allowed, because allow rules are evaluated before deny rules
It's allowed, because the rule with the more specific source always wins
It's denied by the default rules, which run before any custom rule
It's denied, because the deny rule at priority 200 is processed before the allow

explanation: NSG rules are processed in priority order, lowest number first, and processing stops at the first match. The deny at 200 matches the administrator's traffic before the allow at 300 is reached, so RDP is blocked. Neither specificity nor allow versus deny changes that order. The default rules have the highest numbers (65000 and up), so custom rules run before them. To fix this, give the allow rule a lower number than the deny.

prompt: Administrators need RDP and SSH access to Azure VMs that have no public IP addresses. The company doesn't want to expose ports 3389 or 22 to the internet or install any client software. What should it use?

options.text: Azure Web Application Firewall
Azure Bastion
A public IP on each VM, with an NSG rule for the admins
Azure DDoS IP Protection

explanation: Azure Bastion is a platform-managed service deployed in the virtual network that opens RDP and SSH sessions from the Azure portal over TLS, reaching the VMs on their private IPs, so they need no public IP, agent or special client. Public IPs with NSG rules still expose the management ports to the internet. WAF protects web applications over HTTP, and DDoS IP Protection mitigates floods against public IPs; neither provides remote access.

prompt: Developers keep a database connection string, a third-party API key and a TLS certificate in configuration files in source control. The security team wants these kept centrally, with access controlled and logged. Which Azure service should hold them?

options.text: Microsoft Defender for Cloud
Azure Key Vault
Microsoft Purview Information Protection
Azure Storage with a shared access signature

explanation: Azure Key Vault centrally stores and manages secrets such as connection strings and API keys, cryptographic keys and certificates, including certificate renewal. Access is controlled through Microsoft Entra ID and RBAC and logged for auditing, and keys can be protected by hardware security modules. A storage account with a SAS token is just another credential to protect. Purview labels and protects documents and email, and Defender for Cloud assesses posture rather than storing secrets.

prompt: A company has just onboarded its Azure subscriptions to Microsoft Defender for Cloud and hasn't enabled any paid plan. Which TWO capabilities does it already get? (Select TWO.)

options.text: A secure score that summarizes its security posture
Threat detection alerts for its virtual machines
Hardening recommendations based on the Microsoft cloud security benchmark
Malware scanning of the files uploaded to its storage accounts
Attack path analysis across its cloud resources

explanation: Foundational CSPM is free and turned on at onboarding: asset discovery, continuous assessment against the Microsoft cloud security benchmark, which is assigned by default, hardening recommendations and the secure score. Attack path analysis and the cloud security explorer are part of the paid Defender CSPM plan. Threat alerts for VMs and malware scanning of uploads are workload protection features of Defender for Servers and Defender for Storage.

prompt: A company's Azure SQL databases and virtual machines are already assessed for misconfigurations in Defender for Cloud. It now wants security alerts when someone attempts SQL injection or brute-forces logins against them. What does it need to enable?

options.text: Governance rules that assign recommendations to resource owners
The Defender plans for those resource types (workload protection)
The regulatory compliance dashboard with ISO 27001 added to it
A custom security initiative with more Azure Policy definitions

explanation: Posture management finds weaknesses, but detecting attacks in progress is the job of cloud workload protection, delivered through Defender plans per resource type, such as Defender for Servers and Defender for Databases. When a plan detects a threat, it raises a security alert with its severity and remediation steps. Initiatives, compliance standards and governance rules all work on recommendations about configuration, not on live threats.

prompt: When Microsoft Sentinel creates a high-severity incident about a compromised account, the SOC wants the account disabled, a ticket opened in its IT service management tool and the on-call analyst notified, all without human action. Which Sentinel capability should it use?

options.text: A workbook that charts incidents by severity
An automation rule that runs a playbook
A hunting query saved as a bookmark
A data connector for the IT service management tool

explanation: This is the SOAR side of Sentinel. Automation rules react to incidents based on conditions such as severity and can trigger playbooks, which are workflows built on Azure Logic Apps that take actions like disabling the account, opening a ticket and sending notifications. Workbooks visualize data, hunting queries look proactively for threats that no rule has caught, and data connectors bring data into Sentinel rather than acting on incidents.

prompt: A company ingests its firewall, Microsoft Entra ID and AWS CloudTrail logs into Microsoft Sentinel. It wants Sentinel to query that data on a schedule, raise alerts when it finds suspicious patterns and group related alerts into incidents. Which feature does this?

options.text: Notebooks
Workbooks
Data connectors
Analytics rules

explanation: Analytics rules are Sentinel's detections: they run queries against the collected data on a schedule, generate alerts when they find suspicious activity and group related alerts into incidents for the team to investigate. Data connectors are how the firewall, Entra ID and CloudTrail data got into Sentinel in the first place. Workbooks are dashboards for visualizing data, and notebooks support advanced hunting and analysis led by an analyst rather than scheduled detection.

prompt: Several phishing emails reached users' Exchange Online inboxes before Microsoft updated its verdict on them. The company wants such messages to be moved out of inboxes automatically after delivery. Which Microsoft Defender for Office 365 feature does this?

options.text: Message trace
Zero-hour auto purge (ZAP)
Safe Attachments
Attack simulation training

explanation: Zero-hour auto purge acts retroactively: when a message already delivered to an Exchange Online mailbox is later identified as phishing, spam or malware, ZAP moves it to junk or quarantine. Safe Attachments detonates attachments in a sandbox before delivery, so it acts too early to catch these. Attack simulation training runs fake phishing campaigns to train users, and message trace shows the path and status of a message without changing it.

prompt: A SOC wants to detect pass-the-hash, reconnaissance against Active Directory and other lateral movement involving its on-premises domain controllers, using sensors installed on those servers. Which service fits?

options.text: Microsoft Entra ID Protection
Microsoft Defender for Identity
Microsoft Defender for Office 365
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps

explanation: Defender for Identity uses sensors on domain controllers and on AD FS and AD CS servers to read events and network traffic, builds behavioral baselines and detects reconnaissance, compromised credentials, lateral movement and domain dominance. Entra ID Protection works on cloud sign-ins and user risk in Entra ID, not on on-premises AD traffic. Defender for Cloud Apps covers SaaS apps, and Defender for Office 365 covers email and collaboration tools.

prompt: A company suspects employees are uploading work files to file-sharing and AI apps that IT never approved. It wants to find out which cloud apps are in use, see a risk assessment for each and mark risky ones as unsanctioned. Which service should it use?

options.text: Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management
Microsoft Defender for Cloud
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps
Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager

explanation: Defender for Cloud Apps is Microsoft's cloud access security broker (CASB). Its cloud discovery analyzes traffic logs against a catalog of thousands of apps, scores each on more than 90 risk factors and lets you sanction or unsanction them, which is how you tackle shadow IT. Defender for Cloud protects your own Azure and multicloud resources, Compliance Manager tracks regulatory controls, and Vulnerability Management finds weaknesses on devices.

prompt: A security team gets thousands of CVEs from scans of its laptops and servers. It wants them prioritized by active exploitation, breach likelihood and how critical each device is, and wants to send remediation tasks to IT through Intune. Which solution does this?

options.text: Microsoft Sentinel workbooks
Microsoft Entra ID Governance
Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager
Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management

explanation: Defender Vulnerability Management inventories software, certificates, firmware and browser extensions across devices, and prioritizes weaknesses using Microsoft threat intelligence, breach likelihood, business context and device assessments. It can create remediation tasks in Microsoft Intune and track their progress. Sentinel workbooks only chart data you already have, Compliance Manager tracks regulatory controls, and ID Governance manages access rights, not software flaws.

prompt: A SOC is moving its daily work to the Microsoft Defender portal. Which TWO things can analysts do there? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Download Microsoft's SOC 2 audit reports for the cloud services it uses
Make administrators eligible for Microsoft Entra roles through PIM
Work one incident that groups related alerts from endpoints, email, identities and apps
Run advanced hunting queries across Defender XDR and Microsoft Sentinel data
Publish retention labels to users' mailboxes and OneDrive accounts

explanation: The Defender portal is Microsoft's unified security operations portal: Defender XDR correlates alerts from its services into one incident that tells the whole attack story, and advanced hunting runs KQL queries across that data and, once Sentinel is onboarded to the portal, across Sentinel data too. Retention labels are published from the Microsoft Purview portal, PIM assignments are made in the Microsoft Entra admin center, and audit reports come from the Service Trust Portal.

prompt: An analyst working in the Defender portal wants Microsoft's report on a newly tracked ransomware group: who it targets, the techniques it uses, related indicators of compromise and whether the organization has active alerts or exposed devices linked to it. Where should the analyst look?

options.text: Cloud discovery in Defender for Cloud Apps
The secure score page in Defender for Cloud
Activity explorer in Microsoft Purview
Threat analytics, under Threat intelligence

explanation: Threat analytics reports, in the Threat intelligence section of the Defender portal, analyze threats and actors that Microsoft tracks and include guidance on defending against them; each report also uses your own data to show related alerts and how exposed your devices are. Intel profiles and Intel explorer add actor details and indicators. Secure score measures posture, Activity explorer tracks actions on labeled content, and cloud discovery finds the SaaS apps people use.

prompt: An external auditor asks a company for independent audit reports, such as ISO 27001 and SOC 2, that show how Microsoft secures the cloud services the company uses. Where can the company get them?

options.text: The regulatory compliance dashboard in Defender for Cloud
Compliance Manager in the Microsoft Purview portal
The Microsoft Service Trust Portal
The audit log in Microsoft Purview Audit

explanation: The Service Trust Portal is where Microsoft publishes audit reports produced by independent auditors, along with whitepapers and compliance guides on how its cloud services protect data; some documents require signing in with an organizational account. Compliance Manager and the Defender for Cloud dashboard assess your own configuration against standards, and Purview Audit records user and admin activity in your tenant, not Microsoft's certifications.

prompt: A compliance officer must show progress toward ISO 27001 for the company's Microsoft 365 environment. She wants a prebuilt assessment, step-by-step actions she can assign to colleagues with evidence attached, and a view of which controls Microsoft already handles. Which solution should she use?

options.text: The Microsoft Service Trust Portal
Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management
Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager
Microsoft Purview eDiscovery

explanation: Compliance Manager offers assessments built from templates for hundreds of regulations and standards, improvement actions you can assign, test and document with evidence, and a split between your controls, shared controls and Microsoft-managed controls. Its compliance score shows progress. The Service Trust Portal only publishes Microsoft's own audit reports, eDiscovery finds content for legal cases, and Insider Risk Management looks for risky user activity.

prompt: Management asks what the compliance score in Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager actually measures. Which TWO statements are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: It only counts the controls that the organization implements by itself
It tracks completed improvement actions, each worth points based on its risk
A score of 100% certifies that the organization complies with the regulation
It includes points for actions Microsoft completed as the cloud provider
It's calculated from the number of open security alerts in the Defender portal

explanation: Compliance Manager awards points for completed improvement actions, with values that depend on the risk involved, and the score combines your points with Microsoft-managed points for actions Microsoft already handles as the provider. It helps you prioritize and track progress, but it isn't a certification: only an auditor or regulator can determine that you comply. Security alerts feed Defender XDR incidents, not the compliance score.

prompt: A company wants documents classified as Confidential to be encrypted so that only employees can open them, to show a "Confidential" header and to keep that protection even after they're emailed outside the company. What should it use?

options.text: SharePoint site permissions limited to employees
Sensitivity labels, published through a label policy
Retention labels applied to each of the documents
A DLP policy that blocks all external sharing

explanation: Sensitivity labels classify content and can apply encryption that travels with the file wherever it goes, plus content markings such as headers, footers and watermarks. Label policies publish the labels to users and can set a default label or require a justification to lower one. Retention labels decide how long content is kept, a DLP policy that blocks sharing would stop the email instead of protecting the file, and site permissions don't follow a file once it leaves the site.

prompt: A bank wants to warn users with a policy tip when they try to share a document containing credit card numbers outside the company in Exchange, SharePoint or Teams, and to block copying such files to USB drives on Windows devices. What should it configure?

options.text: A Conditional Access policy that blocks unmanaged devices
An insider risk management policy for data leaks
A retention policy for the Exchange and SharePoint locations
A Microsoft Purview DLP policy that also covers devices

explanation: Data loss prevention policies detect sensitive information types, such as credit card numbers, in email, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams and, with endpoint DLP, on Windows and macOS devices, and can show policy tips, block actions or let users override with a justification. Insider risk management correlates many signals to find risky users rather than enforcing a rule on each action. Retention keeps or deletes content, and Conditional Access controls sign-ins, not what's inside files.

prompt: A company keeps everything in a SharePoint site for five years with a retention policy, but its signed contracts must be kept for ten years and declared as records. Which TWO statements about retention labels apply to this plan? (Select TWO.)

options.text: The site's retention policy will delete the contracts after five years
Retention labels can only be applied to whole sites and mailboxes
A retention label can give individual items, such as each contract, ten-year retention
An item can carry several retention labels at once, one for each regulation that applies
A retention label can mark an item as a record, which restricts edits and deletion

explanation: Retention policies set the same retention for a whole location such as a site or mailbox, while retention labels work item by item and can declare an item a record, which blocks certain edits and deletion and keeps proof of disposition. A labeled contract is kept for the longer period, so the five-year policy doesn't delete it early. Each item can carry only one retention label at a time, and labels apply to items, not to whole sites.

prompt: A compliance admin wants to see which users changed a document's sensitivity label from Confidential to Public last month, and which labeled files were copied to USB drives. Which tool should she use?

options.text: Activity explorer
Microsoft Purview Data Map
Content explorer
Compliance Manager

explanation: Activity explorer shows what users do with labeled and classified content over time, such as label changes and downgrades and, with endpoint DLP signals, file copies to removable media or printing. Content explorer shows a current snapshot of where labeled or sensitive items are and, with special permissions, their contents, but not the history of actions. Compliance Manager tracks regulatory controls, and Data Map catalogs data sources for data governance.

prompt: HR has noticed that some employees download large amounts of customer data in the weeks before they resign. The company wants alerts that correlate resignation dates from an HR connector with unusual downloads, while keeping user names pseudonymized for investigators. Which solution fits?

options.text: Microsoft Purview Audit (Standard)
Microsoft Entra access reviews
Microsoft Defender for Identity
Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management

explanation: Insider Risk Management uses policy templates such as data theft by departing users, combines signals from Microsoft 365, devices and an HR connector, and raises alerts on risky activity. Privacy is built in: user names can be pseudonymized and access to cases is controlled by role. Defender for Identity looks for attacks on Active Directory, Audit records activity without scoring risk, and access reviews recertify access rather than spotting data theft.

prompt: Investigators need to find out who deleted a set of files from a SharePoint site ten months ago. The company only has Audit (Standard). What should it know about this request?

options.text: Audit (Standard) keeps records for 10 years, so a search will find the deletions
The audit log must be turned on site by site before any record is created
Audit (Standard) keeps records for 180 days, so the events are already gone
SharePoint file activity isn't audited, so it has to use eDiscovery instead

explanation: Audit (Standard) is on by default and keeps records for 180 days, so activity from ten months ago is already gone. Audit (Premium) keeps Entra ID, Exchange, OneDrive and SharePoint records for one year by default and supports retention policies of up to 10 years with an add-on license. SharePoint file deletions are audited events, and eDiscovery searches content such as documents and mail for legal cases, not a log of who did what.
